# Command reference

`align --help` shows five entries. Everything else is here, still runs, and is hidden from
the help on purpose (ALI-951): the bare command is the product, the rest are escape hatches.

The two blocks below are generated from the command registry by `npm run docs:commands`; a
test fails when they drift. `(cloud)` in a description marks a command that addresses the
hosted gateway and is not routed to a local graph - see [local-mode.md](local-mode.md).

<!-- commands:start - generated by `npm run docs:commands`, do not edit by hand -->
## Everyday

What `align --help` shows.

```
align                         Set up, or see your graph and what to do next

align ask <query>             Ask a question about your decision graph, or pass a file path to find related decisions
                              flags: --env --limit --repo --all --json

align connect [connectors]    Connect a source and import its decisions. No source: pick from a list. --all: scan every connected cloud connector
                              flags: --env --source --token --yes --json --all --channel --project --from --to --approve
align connect list            List import jobs
                              flags: --env --status --connector
align connect suggestions     List pending import suggestions
                              flags: --env --job --status
align connect scan-runs       List historical scan runs
                              flags: --env
align connect git             Import local git commit history (no auth required)
                              flags: --limit --from --to --branch --approve --env
align connect docs            Import ADRs and your CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md content (no auth required)
                              flags: --limit --approve --env
align connect github          Import your GitHub PRs and issues
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --repo --all --approve --env
align connect gitlab          Import your GitLab merge requests
                              flags: --token --personal --domain --limit --approve --env
align connect linear          Import your Linear issues (personal API token)
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --approve --env
align connect jira            Import your Jira issues
                              flags: --email --token --personal --domain --limit --approve --env
align connect confluence      Import your Confluence pages
                              flags: --email --token --personal --domain --limit --approve --env
align connect slack           Import decision threads from Slack (xoxp- user token) [experimental]
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --days-back --approve --env
align connect teams           Import channel messages from Microsoft Teams
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --approve --env
align connect zoom            Import cloud recording transcripts from Zoom
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --approve --env
align connect notion          Import your Notion pages (internal integration token)
                              flags: --token --personal --limit --approve --env
align connect sessions        Review decision-shaped moments from local coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, pi, Codex CLI, opencode) one by one
                              flags: --limit --env
align import                  alias of align connect, deprecated - prints one line on stderr per run

align check                   Check current changes against the decision graph (exit 1 = conflict found)
                              flags: --env --all --hook --advisory --format --block-on-critical --adjudicate-deferred --ci --json --title --base --depth --resolve

align mcp                     Run Align as an MCP server for any MCP-capable agent (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, Codex, Gemini, ...)
                              flags: --env --setup --install --remove
```

## Everything else

Hidden from `align --help`; every one still runs.

```
# Set or show the default environment

align env                     Get or set the default environment (local, preview, prod)
align env set <env>           Set the default environment for all commands
align env get                 Show the current default environment

# Usage telemetry on, off, status

align telemetry               Manage anonymous usage telemetry consent for local-only mode
align telemetry on            Opt in to anonymous usage pings in local-only mode
align telemetry off           Opt out of anonymous usage pings in local-only mode
align telemetry status        Show the effective telemetry state and why

# Cloud account sign-in

align login                   Authenticate with Align
                              flags: --env --token

align logout                  Clear stored credentials
                              flags: --env

align whoami                  Show current authenticated user and tenant
                              flags: --env

# Guided onboarding (bare `align` runs it)

align setup                   Guided onboarding: connect your tools and configure MCP in one command
                              flags: --env --approve --local --reset

# Invite a teammate to your graph

align invite <email>          Invite a teammate to your shared Align decision graph
                              flags: --env

# Capture one decision from a URL

align capture <url>           Capture a decision from a URL (Slack/Jira/GitHub/Confluence/etc.)
                              flags: --env

# Keyword search, ranked list

align search <query>          Search the decision graph
                              flags: --env --limit --repo --all

# List and show decisions

align decisions               Browse and inspect decisions in the graph
align decisions list          List decisions
                              flags: --env --platform --status --space --repo --all --limit --unratified --json
align decisions show <id>     Show full detail for a decision
                              flags: --env

# Export decisions as a brief or JSON

align export [topic]          Export decisions as a structured brief. Optionally filter by topic.
                              flags: --env --format --limit --json

# List spaces (cloud)

align spaces                  Manage spaces (project scopes for organizing decisions)
align spaces list             List all spaces
                              flags: --env

# Cross-tool decision relationships

align links                   Browse decision relationships and conflicts
align links list              List decision links
                              flags: --env --relation --decision --json

# Decisions that may be out of date (cloud)

align drift                   Show org-wide drift summary (decisions that may be out of date)
                              flags: --env

# What your graph has done for you

align status                  Show what your decision graph has done for you (value readout)
                              flags: --env

# Write decisions to .align/decisions.md

align context                 Manage the decisions file agents read (.align/decisions.md)
align context sync            Write current decisions to .align/decisions.md and import it from CLAUDE.md
                              flags: --env --limit

# Answer a check the judge declined to rule on

align adjudicate <event-id>   Answer an alignment check that reached the judge and declined to rule. The event id is printed by the failing check.
                              flags: --verdict --note --env

# Stand behind an agent-made decision

align ratify <id>             Stand behind an agent-made decision as a human: mark it as governing, not just said
                              flags: --env

# Promote one ratified local decision to the shared graph

align push <id>               Promote one ratified local decision to the shared graph (per item, after align ratify)
                              flags: --env

# The local graph: start, status, reset, forget

align local                   Manage your local decision graph (no account needed)
align local start             Initialize local decision graph
align local status            Show local graph statistics
align local forget [connector]
                              Remove saved read-only tokens (all, or one named connector)
align local reset             Wipe local graph and reset config
```
<!-- commands:end -->

## Notes

`ask`, `search` and `decisions list` take `--repo <name>` and `--all` in local mode - see
[local-mode.md](local-mode.md#how-the-local-graph-behaves). Without either, they default to
the repo you are standing in (plus anything not attributed to a repo), never to every repo
you have ever imported.

`align connect` with no source opens the same picker `align setup` uses. `align connect
<source>` runs that source's import directly; `align connect --source <id> --token <token>
--yes` does the same with no prompt, for a script or an agent, and `--json` on that form
prints one summary line. `align import ...` is the old spelling: it still works, prints one
deprecation line on stderr, and is removed two minor releases after 0.38.0.

`--json` prints one JSON document on stdout for `check` (the same shape as `--ci`), `ask`
(the matching decisions, no prose answer), `connect --source`, `decisions list`, `links list`
and `export`.

An agent-made decision enters your local graph as a CLAIM (`decider_kind: agent`), never as
a fact the next agent treats as settled. `align decisions list --unratified` shows the
queue; `.align/decisions.md` and the local MCP server both label an unratified claim
`agent-decided, unratified` so an agent reading either can tell a claim from a rule.
`align ratify <id>` is the human act - it refuses a hook, a pipe, or any caller not at a
terminal - and `align push <id>` promotes one ratified local decision to the shared graph,
per item, never bulk.

See [Cloud or local-only](local-mode.md#telemetry) for what each mode actually sends.
